name: Taganrog Fortress
scope: Troitskoy, the early Taganrog Fortress and its stone harbor moles, as surveyed in December 1704. The model covers the cape-top earthwork, ravelins, four landward fronts, two timber bridges and the near harbor.
era: The December 1704 survey stage, displayed in 1705 before later harbor and town changes.

publicDomainEvidence.sourceCitation: [https://books.google.com/books?id=4QcEAAAAYAAJ Robert Lyall, '''Travels in Russia, the Krimea, the Caucasus, and Georgia''', Volume 2]

originalReview.notes: The exact Qualla original shows the later town over the old fort, the harbor and sea-facing cape. Used only as an independent shoreline and harbor cross-check. The 1825 publication date and Lyall’s lifetime are recorded by the original publication and the Providence Athenaeum catalogue.

externalReferences.artist: An engineer of Troitskoy serving under Johan Jacob Breckling
externalReferences.archiveCitation: Russian State Archive of Ancient Acts, fond 9, inventory 2, file 66, no. 34

originalReview.notes: Exact planar reproduction matches handwriting, paper seams, inscriptions, earlier colors and edge defects of Avakov’s independently published plate. The original manuscript is dated and signed by Breckling. The historical dossier identifies its draughtsman as one of his engineers. Only the 1704 drawing is used.

review.method: Inspected exact Qualla print and matched independent copies of the dated archival manuscript.
review.notes: Started with the Qualla hero, the exact Commons original of Robert Lyall’s 1825 plate. It corroborates the cape and harbor. Modern museum reconstruction and modern port images were omitted. Supplemented with the date-signed 1704 survey of Troitskoy after matching the high-resolution archival reproduction against Avakov’s journal plate.
